data.title: Frasers Logistics DPU stalls at 2.95 cents despite 6.7% revenue gain
data.description:
Adjusted net property income climbed 9.6% to $180.6m in the same six months.

Frasers Logistics and Commercial Trust’s distribution per unit (DPU) remained unchanged at $0.0295 for the second half of 2026 (2H2026), despite higher revenue, its manager reported.

For the financial year 2026 (FY2026), DPU declined 0.8% year on year (YoY) to $0.059, from $0.0595 in the previous year.

However, FY2026 DPU before capital distribution of divestment gains rose 9.4% YoY to 5.70 cents, translating to an annualised distribution yield of 6.7%.

Meanwhile, the trust’s revenue grew 6.7% YoY to $255.2m in H2 2026, from $239.2m. For the full year, revenue increased 4.8% to $494.1m, from $471.5m.

Adjusted net property income also rose, climbing 9.6% YoY to $180.6m in H2 2026 and 6.6% to $347.6m for FY2026.

The manager attributed the growth to higher annual rental increments in the logistics and industrial segment and stronger average Australian dollar and euro exchange rates against the Singapore dollar.

Contributions from acquisitions involving interests in four logistics properties in Germany and the Netherlands also drove the growth.

These gains were partially offset by higher finance costs arising from increased interest rates, the September 2025 divestment of 357 Collins Street, and higher non-recoverable land taxes in Victoria and Queensland, Australia.

For H2 2026, divestment gains amounted to $109.5m, up from $101.8m in H2 2025. This reflected lower income tax expenses, partly offset by a lower proportion of management fees, and higher finance costs.

Meanwhile, distributable income before capital distribution of divestment gains rose to S$216.4m in FY2026, from S$196.8m in FY2025.

data.title: Hugel targets wider Singapore demand beyond aesthetics
data.description:
Clinical trials could broaden botulinum toxin demand beyond cosmetic treatments.

Hugel Inc. is looking to widen demand for its botulinum toxin products in Singapore beyond aesthetic medicine as it develops additional therapeutic indications.

In an interview during the 2026 Gangwon Biohealth Press Tour, Lee Yeon Kyung, Director and Production Group 2 Leader at Hugel, said the company is conducting clinical trials for uses including ptosis correction and polio treatment, alongside applications such as square-jaw reduction.

The shift could expand the product’s addressable market beyond cosmetic procedures and into a broader range of clinical settings.

Hugel already exports its botulinum toxin products to Singapore, giving the company an existing market base for any future expansion in approved indications.

“We are currently exporting our products to the Singapore market, and as far as I know, we have not received any complaints from Singapore,” Lee said.

She added that Hugel’s manufacturing base in South Korea benefits from pharmaceutical production standards, specialised facilities and trained workers for injectable medicines.

Lee cited Korean good manufacturing practice requirements as part of that manufacturing foundation.

“I believe our strength lies in the fact that these are pharmaceuticals you can trust and rely on,” she said.

For healthcare providers and distributors, the commercial significance lies in whether botulinum toxin can move beyond its established cosmetic use and gain wider uptake for therapeutic applications.

Any expansion in Singapore would still depend on the outcome of ongoing clinical trials and the regulatory acceptance of additional indications.

For Hugel, the next stage of growth in the market is therefore less about entering Singapore and more about widening where and how its existing products can be used.

data.title: Korean pet diagnostics firm targets Singapore market
data.description:
The urinary tract infection patch has completed R&D but remains at the prototype stage.

A South Korean pet diagnostics developer is exploring Singapore as a potential export market for an at-home urinary tract infection testing patch that has completed research and development but has yet to launch commercially.

Lee Se Hyuk, Team leader of Ustation Inc., said in an interview during the 2026 Gangwon Biohealth Press Tour that the patch is designed to allow pet owners to screen for urinary tract infections without first visiting a veterinary clinic.

“With our patch, you can easily diagnose urinary tract infections in your pets at home,” the company representative said.

The product remains in the prototype stage. Although research and development has been completed, it has not yet been officially launched in South Korea.

The company has also yet to enter any export markets, making its Singapore plans part of an early-stage international expansion effort. Its target markets are countries with relatively high levels of pet ownership, where home-based animal health monitoring could support demand for new diagnostic products.

Singapore is among the markets being considered because of its developed healthcare sector and potential demand for technology-led health products.

“Our goal is to enter that market with products that can definitely succeed there, thanks to our Korean technology,” the representative said.

The company is using trade shows in Singapore to assess potential opportunities before entering the market.

For distributors and veterinary businesses, the commercial question is whether at-home testing can complement clinic-based diagnostics and support earlier screening.

However, any market entry would depend on moving the product from prototype to commercial launch, establishing distribution and meeting local regulatory requirements.

data.title: Gangwon biohealth firms eye Singapore for ASEAN growth
data.description:
Export-led Korean biotech companies see Singapore as a route to regional markets.

Gangwon biohealth and medical device companies are looking to Singapore as they pursue overseas growth, reflecting the export-heavy business model of South Korea’s biotech sector.

Speaking at the 2026 Gangwon Biohealth Press Tour, Kim Kyoung Hwan, Director of the Strategy Planning Division at Chuncheon Bioindustry Foundation, said many South Korean medical device and biotech companies generate most of their revenue overseas and target global markets from an early stage.

“In many cases, South Korean medical device and biotech companies generate most of their revenue overseas rather than in the domestic market,” Kim said.

That makes Singapore commercially relevant because of its position as an ASEAN hub and its role in connecting companies to regional markets.

Gangwon’s competitive position, meanwhile, is built on long-term policy support and research funding. Kim described the province as having “institutional thickness,” with government programmes helping companies strengthen technological capabilities and prepare for larger-scale production.

He said that foundation gives firms an advantage when moving from product development into scale-up and economies of scale.

For Singapore-based companies, the potential opportunity lies in working with Gangwon firms on raw-material trade, technology collaboration and new market development.

“Biotech companies in Gangwon Province and companies in Singapore can grow together in various ways,” Kim said.

The commercial case is therefore less about direct competition and more about linking Gangwon’s technology and production capabilities with Singapore’s regional market access.

data.title: F&B sales rise 1% as fast food leads growth
data.description:
Fast-food turnover increased 7.6%, whilst food courts and other eating places recorded a 4.2% decline.

Food and beverage services sales rose 1% YoY in September 2026, reversing the 1.8% contraction recorded in August.

On a seasonally adjusted basis, sales increased 0.8% from the previous month, according to the Department of Statistics.

The total value of F&B sales was estimated at $1.6b. Online transactions accounted for approximately 21.1% of the total, slightly higher than the 20.9% share recorded in August.

Fast-food outlets posted the strongest performance, with sales up 7.6% YoY.

Restaurant turnover grew 2.6%, whilst cafe sales edged up 0.1%.

By contrast, food caterers registered a 0.2% YoY decline. Food courts and other eating places recorded the largest contraction at 4.2%.

On a seasonally adjusted monthly basis, cafe sales increased 3.6%, while food caterers recorded 3% growth.

Turnover at restaurants and fast-food outlets rose 1.1% each from August.

Food courts and other eating places were the only F&B segment to record a monthly decline, with sales falling 2.4%.

data.title: Bruno Gallery brings Picasso, Miró, Dalí and Chagall to Singapore
data.description:
The 36 pieces lead with signed etchings and lithographs, priced from $18,000.

Bruno Gallery Singapore has launched its latest exhibition showcasing works of four artists who made their mark in Paris.

Running until 30 November, ‘From Spain to France: Four Masters Who Changed Modern Art’ features 36 works by Pablo Picasso, Joan Miró, Salvador Dalí and Marc Chagall. Arriving in Paris from different corners of Europe, the four artists collectively expanded what art could depict and how it could be seen in the first decades of the 20th century.

“Picasso, Miró, Dalí and Chagall did not speak the same visual language, and that is precisely what makes bringing them together so compelling,” said Motti Abramovitz, owner and chief executive of Bruno Gallery Singapore.

“Looking at their works together also allows us to see the connections between artists and movements that we often encounter separately,” Abramovitz said, adding that for Singapore audiences, the exhibition is an opportunity to experience those artistic relationships through the works themselves, whilst for collectors, it brings together important names in modern art within a single presentation.

The exhibition leads with printmaking, a medium that allowed ideas developed in painting and drawing to circulate in distinct and often more intimate forms. Signed etchings by Picasso and Dalí and signed lithographs by Miró and Chagall are on view; catalogue prices begin at $18,000.

The nine Picasso works featured in the exhibition include signed etchings such as Mask, Joker and two untitled compositions. Meanwhile, the 13 Miró works include Passage de L’Égyptienne, Homage to Miró, Cercle Rompu and Plate II from Espriu.

For Dalí, his eight featured works are original etchings from The Hippies series, amongst them Woman in Waves, Corridor of Kathmandu, Flower Woman at the Piano and Nude with Garter.

The six Chagall works include Le Clown à la Flûte I, Le Cirque (Acrobats), Le Clown Blanc and Elijah Resurrects the Son of the Widow of Zarephath.

‘From Spain to France: Four Masters Who Changed Modern Art’ is on at Bruno Gallery, 91 Tanglin Road, #01-03 Tanglin Place until 30 November. Admission is free.

data.title: Singapore retail sales rise 1.7% YoY in September
data.description:
Computer and telecommunications equipment saw the strongest growth at 16.5%

Singapore's retail sales rose 1.7% year-on-year (YoY) in September, accelerating from the 0.8% growth recorded in August, according to the Department of Statistics Singapore.

Excluding motor vehicles, parts and accessories, retail sales increased 2.5%, compared with 1.7% growth in August.

On a seasonally adjusted month-on-month basis, sales declined 1% in September. Excluding motor vehicles, parts and accessories, sales fell 1.8%.

Amongst retail categories, computer and telecommunications equipment recorded the strongest YoY growth at 16.5%, mainly driven by higher demand for mobile phones.

Petrol service stations recorded a 6.5% increase, largely due to higher petrol prices, whilst sales of cosmetics, toiletries and medical goods grew 6%.

In contrast, mini-marts and convenience stores saw a 5.6% decline in sales, whilst department store sales also fell 3.4%.

data.title: Former minister George Yeo buys $297,000 worth of Wilmar stake
data.description:
He acquired 100,000 shares, raising his total holding to 1.01 million.

Former Singapore minister and Wilmar International independent director George Yong-Boon Yeo acquired 100,000 shares in the company for $297,000 through a market transaction on 4 November.

Yeo's direct shareholding in Wilmar increased from 906,500 shares, or 0.015%, to 1,006,500 shares, or 0.016%, according to a bourse filing.

The percentages were calculated based on Wilmar's 6.24 billion voting shares, excluding treasury shares, as at 4 November.

The shares were purchased at an average price of $2.97 apiece, excluding brokerage and stamp duties.

data.title: CAREIT beats forecast with $117.7m net property income in 9M
data.description:
Gross revenue exceeds expectations by 5.7% at $164.4m

Centurion Accommodation REIT (CAREIT) posted a better-than-expected nine-month (9M) performance with a net property income (NPI) of $117.7m in its business update on 4 November.

CAREIT’s NPI exceeded Prospectus Forecast by 4.8%. The firm also recorded gross revenue of $164.4m, higher by 5.7% than predicted.

The REIT’s third-quarter (Q3) performance also grew, with gross revenue of $55.5m and NPI of $39.3m, beating forecast by 6.9% and 5.7%, respectively.

The firm attributed outperformance to higher rental rates across its Purpose-Built Worker Accommodation (PBWA) portfolio in Singapore and higher occupancy at its Westlife chain.

CAREIT also said additional revenue contributions from Toh Guan Expanded Capacity (TEC) and Mandai Expanded Capacity (MEC) worth $2.3m drove growth, alongside favourable foreign exchange rates—although partially offset by rental rate moderation and fewer beds for sale.

The REIT’s portfolio currently has 15 assets across Singapore, the UK and Australia, with an operating capacity of 30, 197 beds.

In Singapore, the firm holds five PBWA assets with an operating capacity of 26, 742 beds, which contribute 73.2% of gross revenue and 75.1% of NPI in 9M.

Financial occupancy for the PBWA and Purpose-Built Student Accommodation (PBSA) tallied 92.6% and 95.6%, respectively—in line with Prospectus Forecasts at 93% and 96%.

CAREIT’s PBWA portfolio is driven by new and expanded capacity at Westlife Toh Guan and Westlife Mandai, with average committed occupancy up to 98.1% at the end of September.

Westlife Toh Guan and Westlife Mandai reached 99.7% and 95.1% committed occupancy, respectively.

A new six-storey block is progressing at Westlife Ubi, expected to operate by Q4 2027. It will add 540 beds to the current 1,650-bed capacity.

Westlife Woodlands secured permission for the proposed Asset Enhancement Initiative (AEI) to develop two new blocks, increasing the property’s capacity from approximately 4,100 beds to 5,528 beds by 2029.

The AEI is intended to mitigate capacity reductions. The Interim Dormitory Standards are set to reduce 2030 capacity to 5,190 beds and the New Dormitory Standards are set to reduce that further to 4,506 beds by 2041 onwards.

The REIT said its aggregate leverage stood at 30.7%, with $350m of debt headroom to provide flexibility in pursuit of portfolio growth.

CAREIT expects the financial year to exceed the Prospectus Forecast, driven by rental rates and occupancy across its PBWA portfolio and approximately $3.5m additional revenue from TEC and MEC.

The Centurion Asset Management, manager of CAREIT, said it will focus on completing ramp-up at Westlife Mandai, progressing the six-storey development at Westlife Ubi, advancing AEI at Westlife Woodlands and delivering targeted AEIs at Dwell Hotwells House and Dwell the Grafton.

The manager will continue evaluating AEIs and redevelopment opportunities across the existing PBWA portfolio.

It will also evaluate acquisitions of PBWA and PBSA assets from its sponsor, Centurion Corporation and third parties. The corporation has granted CAREIT a right of first refusal over its stake in assets within the REIT’s investment mandate.
